This semester I did 24 credits, but only 1 course got on my nerves, HRM370. If you're looking forward to bare minimum education and not regular chitchat there's no way you should take TUA sir's course. For this 370, I had to submit 16 hand written assignments for around 130 pages total. Had to submit printed out assignment which essentially have no meaning. There's a thing called Self Skills Development (SSD) in his course, and 99% of the students opt for cooking, dancing, singing. What's the use of learning how to sing for a major HRM course worth 20k? And let alone the impression thing. But at the same time, he can't be blamed alone. Most of the students going for HRM are like that, they would rather make videos of themselves cooking and dancing, and submit it in pendrives to him, instead of studying the littlest to earn grades. Choice will not be between 2 faculties offering the course, the choice will be if you want to spend 30k on a course(20k tuition fee+ 10k for printouts, new dresses, pendrives, etc.) Or get at least a minimum understanding of what managerial skills development course is. If you can keep up with statements like "laptop is like a naked lady, if it's in front of you, your eyes will be on it" during a class, and abide by the "noise of heels means look at me, and which girl doesn't want attention?", then maybe you can go for it. But if you're a person of value, and would rather accept a hard earned grade, instead of a recreational grade, go for anyone else offering the course.
Best of luck!
P.S. there's no guaranteed output at the end of the semester, and I wish I could attach a screenshot of my grades so everyone could see how much disparity is there between 86 credits done under 30 different faculties and 3 credits done under TUA. Ruined my whole portfolio
